blocks.text: Job 10 belongs to the sustained debate that follows seven days in which Job and his friends sit together silently. After Job curses the day of his birth, Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar increasingly explain his suffering as evidence of wrongdoing, while Job rejects that diagnosis. This setting helps explain why Job's anguished questions in this chapter are spoken as part of an unresolved argument rather than as a settled explanation of his suffering.

Job's endurance across the story should not be mistaken for silent submission. His persistence includes voicing complaint and seeking an answer; it is not a rule that requires someone to remain silent in abuse or to forgo escape and protection.
